newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho army quells police mutiny, arrests rebels.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho army quells police mutiny, arrests rebels.

text.p: Lesotho army troops ended an 11-day police mutiny on Sunday, overwhelming the rebels with a dawn onslaught of heavy gunfire that forced at least 30 policemen to surrender.
"Now everything is okay. It is over. They have all been taken," an army major on the scene told Reuters. The army said nobody was hurt.

The leader of the rebels, identified by diplomats as Second Lieutenant Pakiso Molise, and two other rebel officers managed to escape during the shootout and reach the palace of King Letsie III, diplomats said.

"Molise and two comrades were arrested at the palace after the shooting started. They had sought refuge there but they were followed in by the Lesotho Defence Force and arrested," one diplomat told Reuters.

He could not confirm if the constitutional monarch was in the residence in the capital Maseru at the time. King Letsie III pledged to "abstain from involving the monarchy in any way in politics" when he was sworn in as monarch a year ago at the age of 32.
Molise and seven other officers took over the police headquarters in Maseru 11 days ago to demand amnesty for the murder of three fellow officers in 1995.
They "sacked" the police chief and called on Lesotho's 2,000 police to go on a national strike. Most officers heeded the call and it was unclear if they would return to work on Monday.
Throughout the day state radio issued government statements appealing for the public to remain calm. The streets of Maseru returned to normal.

There was no official government reaction to the military operation but it is expected to be raised in parliament on Monday. The rebels were being held at an army base some two km (one mile) outside Maseru.

The heavy gunfire erupted in the southern African capital early on Sunday as troops moved in to end the mutiny. Western diplomats had earlier said the crisis could lead to a coup against Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle's government.

The gun battle raged for five hours with grenade explosions and intermittent gunfire echoing through the city. Lesotho Defence Force soldiers at the main entrance to the capital blocked traffic from entering.
Roads in front of the police building were littered with spent cartridges from heavy machine guns on armoured personnel carriers. Police inside the building returned fire with semi-automatic rifles.
The building was pockmarked and windows were shattered. Onlookers tramped through the offices after the army moved out to see the damage.
The army major told Reuters that soldiers had first tried to negotiate with the rebel police.

"We tried to convince them to come out and that we wouldn't fight them. We started shooting about an hour later to get them out of the offices. We were not trying to kill them but just trying to frighten them," he said.
